title: Faisal Town Phase 2 Master Plan: How Buyers Should Read It
seoTitle: Faisal Town Phase 2 Master Plan – Sectors, Roads & Map Guide
metaDescription: Learn how to read the Faisal Town Phase 2 master plan, identify sectors, roads, amenities and plot locations, and verify a property before booking.
description: A practical guide to reading the Faisal Town-II master plan, comparing sectors, understanding roads and land use, and verifying plots before booking.
intro:
The Faisal Town Phase 2 master plan is one of the first references buyers should use before comparing a plot, sector or enclave.

Start with the full FT-II plan to understand the wider road network and project structure, then move to the relevant sector plan and exact plot reference. A master plan helps with orientation, but it should always be combined with current inventory, documentation and an on-ground check.
body:
## Why the Faisal Town Phase 2 master plan matters

The Faisal Town-II master plan helps buyers understand the project as a whole before focusing on one plot.

FaisalTown Group currently describes Faisal Town-II as an under-development residential community covering approximately 40 million square metres.

That scale matters.

A plot should not be judged only by its size or advertised price. Its position within the wider project can affect:

- access
- road hierarchy
- nearby land use
- commercial activity
- community facilities
- development timing
- practical site access
- future resale comparison

The full master plan therefore comes before the plot-level decision.

## Start with the full Phase 2 master plan

Before opening a cropped sector image, review the complete Faisal Town Phase 2 plan.

Use it to understand:

- the overall project footprint
- major roads
- sector relationships
- commercial areas
- green and open spaces
- community-use areas
- larger project destinations
- possible approach routes

The full plan provides context that a small plot screenshot cannot.

Once you know where the relevant sector sits inside FT-II, move to the dedicated sector plan where available.

## Faisal Town-II is a separate project

Do not confuse the Phase 2 master plan with Faisal Town Phase 1 / F-18 maps.

Phase 1 uses established block references such as:

- Block A
- Block B
- Block B-1
- Block C

Faisal Town-II uses sector, enclave and project-area references.

On this website, detailed Phase 2 guides currently cover:

- Sector O / Model Block
- Sector P / The Caladan
- Sector R
- Sector S
- Sector T
- Overseas Enclave

Using the wrong map can lead to incorrect comparisons of price, location and development.

## Master plan vs sector plan

The full master plan and a sector plan serve different purposes.

### Full master plan

Use the full plan to understand:

- where the sector sits
- major roads
- wider project connections
- commercial and community zones
- relationship with neighboring areas

### Sector plan

Use a sector-specific plan to understand:

- individual plot positions
- internal streets
- road widths
- plot rows
- nearby open spaces
- corner positions
- surrounding land use

A buyer should ideally use both.

## How to find your sector

Begin with the sector or enclave named in the listing.

If the listing says:

- Sector O
- Sector P
- Sector R
- Sector S
- Sector T
- Overseas Enclave

locate that area on the Phase 2 project context first.

Then open the relevant detailed guide or sector plan.

Do not rely on informal labels alone.

If a dealer says “P Block,” “O Block” or another block-style name, confirm whether the actual master-plan reference is a Phase 2 sector.

## Sector O / Model Block

Sector O is often associated in market material with Model Block terminology.

Because several informal labels may appear in listings, confirm the exact:

- sector
- sub-area
- plot number
- map reference

before comparing price.

Do not assume that every property described as “Model Block” has the same payment, development or possession status.

## Sector P / The Caladan

Sector P currently has one of the clearest dedicated plans and commercial offers on this website.

Use its sector-specific plan after reviewing the wider FT-II master plan.

For a Sector P property, check:

- exact plot number
- plot size
- road position
- corner or standard location
- surrounding land use
- current payable amount
- any location premium

Do not apply Sector P's current pricing structure to another Phase 2 sector.

## Sector R

Sector R should first be understood within the full Phase 2 master plan.

Where a dedicated current detailed plan is not available, ask for a marked master-plan reference showing the exact property.

Verify:

- road connection
- surrounding sectors
- plot position
- current development
- exact inventory status

Do not rely on a seller simply saying “Sector R” without showing where the property is located.

## Sector S

Sector S has a dedicated plan on this website.

Use the full FT-II master plan first, then the Sector S plan for:

- internal roads
- plot rows
- open areas
- community-use land
- exact plot matching

The sector plan is more useful than a promotional image when deciding between two plots.

## Sector T

Sector T also has a dedicated sector plan.

As with Sector S, use it only after understanding the sector's position within the wider Phase 2 development.

For a plot-level decision, match:

- plot number
- dimensions
- internal road
- surrounding plots
- nearby open or community areas

with the listing and current documents.

## Overseas Enclave

The Overseas Enclave should also be matched carefully against its dedicated plan and exact enclave reference.

Remote buyers should be particularly cautious about cropped plan screenshots.

Request:

- the full plan
- marked plot location
- current map pin
- fresh video
- exact file or plot reference

before making a payment decision.

## How to read road hierarchy

Not every road shown on a master plan serves the same function.

Look for the difference between:

- main boulevards
- sector roads
- internal streets
- access roads
- service roads where shown

A plot beside a major road may offer better visibility or access, but it can also have different traffic, noise or premium considerations.

A smaller internal street may suit a residential end user differently.

Do not assume “main road” is automatically better.

## Road width and plot value

Road width can materially affect buyer demand.

When comparing plots, ask for the actual road width shown on the relevant plan or current project documentation.

Two plots of the same size may differ because one is:

- on a wider road
- on a corner
- close to a boulevard
- deeper inside the sector
- beside an open area

Map position therefore matters alongside plot size.

## Corner plots

Corner plots can carry a special-location premium.

Before accepting a corner premium, confirm that the plot is actually positioned at the junction shown on the current plan.

Ask for:

- plot number
- marked sector plan
- current premium
- written final payable amount

Do not pay a location premium only because an advertisement says “corner.”

## Park-facing, green-facing and open plots

Listings may use descriptions such as:

- park-facing
- green-facing
- open-facing
- boulevard-facing

Match those claims with the relevant project plan.

A nearby green zone shown on a plan does not necessarily mean every nearby plot qualifies for the same premium category.

The exact plot reference matters.

## Commercial areas

FaisalTown Group currently describes Faisal Town-II as including major commercial components, including a Central Business District and Commercial Center.

Commercial zones can matter to residential buyers because they influence:

- access to shops
- future activity
- traffic
- rental interest
- resale perception

However, being closer to a commercial area is not automatically better for every end user.

Some families may prefer a quieter internal location.

## Central Business District

The developer currently describes a Central Business District within Faisal Town-II as a major commercial and business component.

On a master plan, larger commercial or business areas should be understood as project-level destinations rather than treated as ordinary neighborhood shops.

For investment-oriented buyers, proximity may be attractive.

For end users, compare convenience with expected traffic and activity.

## Sports and recreation areas

FaisalTown Group's current Phase 2 material also describes a Sports City concept with planned facilities such as sports grounds and indoor/outdoor recreational infrastructure.

If a seller claims a plot is “near Sports City,” ask them to mark the location on the current master plan.

Do not rely on marketing distance claims without map context.

## Education areas

The current developer description includes an Education City component within Faisal Town-II.

When reviewing a map, educational or institutional zones may matter to families, but the master plan does not tell you whether every facility is operational today.

Separate:

- planned land use
from
- currently completed facilities

This distinction is important in an under-development project.

## Planned amenities vs completed amenities

A master plan primarily shows intended project structure.

It should not automatically be read as a map of completed infrastructure.

For every important feature, ask:

- Is it planned?
- Is work underway?
- Is it completed?
- Is it operational?
- Is the location still consistent with the current plan?

This is especially important in a project the developer currently describes as under development.

## Development status

The map alone cannot tell you the exact current development condition of a plot.

After reviewing the plan, verify the actual site.

Look for:

- earthwork
- road formation
- road carpeting
- drainage
- utilities
- street identification
- plot demarcation
- machinery
- nearby construction
- actual vehicle access

A planned road and a usable road are not necessarily the same thing today.

## Google Maps vs the master plan

Google Maps and the project master plan answer different questions.

### Google Maps can help with:

- external routes
- approximate travel
- road navigation
- live location pins
- nearby existing places

### The master plan can help with:

- sector layout
- internal roads
- project land use
- plot context
- future planned structure

Use both.

Neither replaces a current site visit.

## How to verify a specific plot

For any plot you are considering, ask for:

1. Project name
2. Sector or enclave
3. Plot number
4. Plot size
5. Street or road
6. Marked plan position
7. Current payment status
8. Development status
9. Outstanding dues
10. Location premiums

The plot shown on the map should match the documents and the plot being shown on site.

## Why cropped screenshots can be misleading

A cropped map can make a property appear closer to:

- a boulevard
- a park
- commercial land
- an entrance
- another premium feature

than it really is.

Ask for both:

- the full master plan
- a marked close-up of the exact property

This gives you context and detail together.

## Master plan vs marketing illustration

A promotional rendering is not the same thing as a master plan.

Architectural images may show how a future area could look.

A master plan is used to understand layout and land-use relationships.

Neither should be treated as proof of:

- current development
- possession
- utility completion
- actual construction progress

Use on-ground evidence for those questions.

## Plot size is only one filter

Do not select a plot only because it is 5.56, 8, 10.89, 14.22 marla or 1 kanal.

For two same-size plots, compare:

- road width
- exact location
- sector
- development
- special-location status
- payment completion
- dues
- total cost

The cheaper plot may not necessarily offer better value.

## Compare like-for-like plots

When comparing two plots, keep the variables as similar as possible.

For example:

- 8 marla vs 8 marla
- same sector where possible
- similar payment status
- similar road category
- similar development status

Otherwise, the comparison can be misleading.

A fully paid plot and a partially paid plot should not be compared using asking price alone.

## Do not use the master plan as a price list

The master plan tells you where property sits.

It does not tell you today's market value.

Price requires separate checks using:

- live inventory
- current seller asking prices
- current developer offers
- outstanding balance
- special-location premium
- transaction costs

Keep location analysis and price analysis separate.

## Do not use the master plan as proof of availability

A numbered plot shown on a plan is not necessarily available for booking today.

Before payment, confirm:

- current inventory
- booking or resale status
- owner or allocation record
- paid amount
- outstanding amount
- transfer eligibility

The map confirms location context, not live availability.

## Verify payment instructions separately

Once you have selected a plot, do not use the map as evidence of where to send money.

FaisalTown Group currently publishes separate official Phase II payment methods through its project resources, including the member portal, challan process and designated company banking channels.

Use current developer documentation and verify the payment recipient before transferring funds.

Do not send money solely from a bank-account screenshot forwarded by an agent.

## Site visit after map review

A practical buying process should be:

1. Open the full Phase 2 master plan.
2. Find the relevant sector.
3. Open the sector plan where available.
4. Mark the exact property.
5. Review current payment details.
6. Visit the location.
7. Compare map and ground conditions.
8. Verify documents.
9. Confirm current payable amount.
10. Only then consider payment.

This order reduces the risk of buying based on marketing material alone.

## Mobile viewing tips

Large master plans can be difficult to read on a phone.

For mobile viewing:

- open the PDF rather than a compressed image
- zoom into the relevant sector
- rotate the phone horizontally
- save a marked screenshot
- keep the full-plan view available for context

Do not make a booking decision from a blurry WhatsApp image.

## Questions to ask your agent

Before shortlisting a plot, ask:

- Which Phase 2 sector is this?
- What is the exact plot number?
- Can you mark it on the full master plan?
- Is there a dedicated sector plan?
- What is the road width?
- Is it corner, boulevard-facing or standard?
- What development is currently complete nearby?
- Is the plot fully paid?
- What dues remain?
- Are location premiums included?
- Is it currently transferable?
- Can I visit the exact location?

Clear answers should be supported by documents and current evidence.

## Download the Phase 2 master plan

Use the full Faisal Town Phase 2 master plan as your project-wide orientation document.

Then use the relevant sector guide for plot-level comparison.

- [Download Faisal Town Phase 2 master plan](/assets/faisal-town-ii/faisal-town-phase-2-master-plan.pdf)
- [Faisal Town Phase 2 guide](/faisal-town-phase-2/)
- [Faisal Town map and location guide](/faisal-town-islamabad-map-location/)

## Final master-plan checklist

Before relying on a master-plan location:

- confirm it is Faisal Town-II
- identify the correct sector
- verify the exact plot number
- use the complete plan
- use the sector plan where available
- check road width
- check surrounding land use
- confirm current development
- confirm current availability
- verify payment status
- inspect the actual site

The master plan is an important buying tool, but it works best when combined with live inventory, documentation and physical verification.

faqsText:
What is the Faisal Town Phase 2 master plan? | The master plan is the project-wide layout used to understand Faisal Town-II sectors, major roads, land-use areas and the relationship between different parts of the development.

Is Faisal Town Phase 2 still under development? | Yes. FaisalTown Group currently describes Faisal Town-II as an under-development residential community. Development can differ by sector and exact location. 

How large is Faisal Town-II? | FaisalTown Group currently lists Faisal Town-II at approximately 40 million square metres. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}

Which Phase 2 sectors are covered on this website? | Current detailed guides cover Sector O / Model Block, Sector P, Sector R, Sector S, Sector T and Overseas Enclave.

Should I use the full master plan or a sector plan? | Use both. Start with the full Phase 2 master plan to understand the wider project, then use the relevant sector plan to identify roads and the exact plot position.

Can a master plan tell me whether a plot is available? | No. A master plan shows layout and location context. Current availability, ownership, booking status and payment position must be verified separately.

Can I use Google Maps instead of the master plan? | No. Google Maps is useful for external routes and current navigation, while the project plan is needed for sector, plot and internal-road context.

Does a park or commercial area shown on the plan mean it is completed? | Not necessarily. Planned land use and current on-ground development are different questions. Verify the current site condition separately.

How do I verify a plot on the map? | Ask for the exact sector, plot number, size and marked plan location, then compare the map with the documents and current on-ground location.

Should I pay after seeing the plot on the master plan? | Not on that basis alone. Verify the property documents, current payment status, dues, transfer or booking position, official payment recipient and site condition before substantial payment.
